aggregate_metrics.ADPR_denominator: All dependency_points unless a paper section explicitly reports primary_async_dependency_ids only.
aggregate_metrics.minimum_success_condition_for_task_level: Both primary_async_dependency_ids pass in the final integrated workspace.

annotation_notes: The backend_to_utilities exception/timeout dependency is the primary async signal because the utilities worker can implement retry and fail_when_locked behavior against stale backend exception semantics.
The flags/fileno dependency captures a second backend contract that can break Lock/RLock integration without textual conflicts.
The semaphore/temporary-file dependency records integration-level lifecycle behavior built on the backend and utilities layers.
These labels identify public test-observable contracts and implicated files, not solution code.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Lock and RLock timeout, fail_when_locked, acquire/release, and retry behavior must consume the platform backend's AlreadyLocked and LockException translation consistently.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when backend exception/conflict probes and utility timeout/acquire probes pass in the integrated workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The utilities worker may handle backend failures as generic exceptions or retry stale non-blocking behavior, passing some local lifecycle tests while failing once final backend exception semantics are integrated.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Utility locks must use shared/exclusive/non-blocking flags and file-object or fileno backend acceptance consistently across direct backend calls and Lock/RLock wrappers.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when direct flag/fileno backend probes and wrapper flag/locker probes pass after integration.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The utilities worker may assume a narrower backend input or flag contract than the final backend supplies, causing clean merges that fail with shared locks, non-blocking validation, or alternative locker implementations.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Temporary-file locks, combined-module use, and bounded semaphores must preserve lock lifecycle, filename selection, cleanup, and acquire/release semantics across the backend and utility artifacts.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when utility acquire/release probes and semaphore/temporary-file integration probes pass in the final workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The utilities artifact may satisfy direct Lock/RLock cases but leave lifecycle or cleanup assumptions inconsistent with semaphore and temporary-file integration.

evaluation_checkpoint_policy.minimum_policy: Run probe tests after each agent final artifact and after final integration.
evaluation_checkpoint_policy.recommended_policy: Run probe tests after every committed patch, every explicit artifact transfer, and final integration.

ADPR.definition: Fraction of registered dependency_points whose required integrated_probe_tests pass in the final integrated workspace.
ADPR.name: Async Dependency Pass Rate

CAIL.definition: downstream_resolution_step minus upstream_resolution_step when both probe groups have been evaluated.
CAIL.name: Cross-Agent Integration Lag

DRS.definition: First recorded checkpoint at which all required integrated_probe_tests for a dependency point pass.
DRS.name: Dependency Resolution Step

SAD.definition: Interval during which a downstream worker acts on a contract assumption inconsistent with the latest upstream artifact visible in the integrated history.
SAD.name: Stale Assumption Duration

purpose: Dependency-level labels for measuring whether asynchronous multi-agent coding resolves Portalocker's POSIX backend and utility-layer contracts promptly.
